prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Co-bottleneck · Framework trade-offs (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Option" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 102px
  col 2: header "Strengths" · longest unbreakable word 72px · one-line width 541px
  col 3: header "Weaknesses" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 646px
  col 4: header "Verdict" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 582px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 581px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare framework options by their strengths, weaknesses, and overall verdict.","reading":"Readers scan the option names, then compare the paired strengths and weaknesses before checking each verdict. Each row should remain easy to follow across the table.","groups":["Strengths and Weaknesses are parallel explanatory columns and should have enough space for readable phrases.","Option and Verdict frame each comparison: one identifies the choice and the other gives its assessment."],"keep_intact":["Individual words and the short verdicts.","Option names where practical, especially when existing row height can accommodate a natural wrap."],"may_wrap":["Strengths and weaknesses can wrap at word boundaries.","Multiword option names can wrap at word boundaries."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [85, 207, 221, 68] · table 582×275px · row heights [33, 94, 73, 73] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [90, 197, 226, 68] · table 582×275px · row heights [33, 94, 73, 73] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [80, 207, 226, 68] · table 582×275px · row heights [33, 94, 73, 73] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
